title: Mixed to 50
subtitle: + − to 50, × ÷ to 12
bounds: Mixed facts (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside + and − to 50 and × and ÷ with factors to 12, easy to hard by tier. Each tier is 6 items from each of facts-add-50, facts-sub-50, facts-mul-12, facts-div-12 at the same tier: the same pools, forms, distractors, explanations and student text, every part's floor n scaled to ceil(n / 4), at most 2 zero-factor multiplication prompts a tier; 24 items per tier, prompts unique per tier, operations interleaved. Misconception keys carry their operation (ADD_, SUB_, MUL_, DIV_). Answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each over the whole tier. [ADD] Facts bounds (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside sums 21 to 50, easy to hard by tier. Prompt forms: R 'a + b = ?' (answer s), C 'a + ? = s' (answer b), S '? + b = s' (answer a); every number a non-negative integer. T1 R, an operand a non-zero multiple of ten. T2 R, no multiple of ten and the ones stay under ten: >= 8 with a one-digit operand, >= 8 with both two-digit. T3 the same with the ones making a ten. T4 C, a, b >= 2, no multiple of ten (>= 12 regrouping). T5 S (>= 12, >= 6 regrouping) and C (>= 6 regrouping), a, b >= 2, no multiple of ten. Prompts unique per tier, 24 per tier. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers <= 999, >= 2 near the answer (+-1, +-2, +-10), at most 1 far; answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each per tier; answers >= 20 always have a wrong choice sharing the ones digit (+-10); the answer is never the only value of its parity. [SUB] Minuends 21-50, a and b at least 2 (T1 allows 1). T1 R with a multiple of 10 as a or b; T2 R no trade (the ones of s at least the ones of a), at least 8 with a one-digit part and 8 with both parts at least 10; T3 R with a trade, same two floors; T4 s − ? = b, at least 12 with a trade, no multiples of 10; T5 ? − a = b (at least 12, 6 with a trade) and s − ? = b (6 with a trade), no multiples of 10. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least two within 1, 2 or 10 of the answer, at most one far; where the answer is 20 or more one wrong choice shares its ones digit; modelled misconceptions first, ARITH only to fill; each answer rank (smallest to largest of the four) holds the answer in 15-35% of a tier. [MUL] Factors 0 to 12. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: the easy rows (0, 1, 2, 5, 10) and 11 times a digit, at least 8 with an 11 or 12 factor (117 prompts); T2 R: a 12 times 3, 4 or 9 (at least 6), 3-4-9 facts (at least 6), else a 3, 4 or 9 fact (33 prompts); T3 R: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 8), 6-7-8 facts (at least 6), else a 6, 7 or 8 fact (37); T4 C: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), 3-4-6-9 core facts (at least 8), else factors 2-12 (121); T5 S: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), any hard fact with factors 3-12 (at least 6), plus C (at least 4 with an 11 or 12; 104 prompts in all). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far; with a factor of 11 or more and an answer of 20 or more, one wrong value shares the answer's ones digit. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier. [DIV] PROTOCOL 4c, facts range cartridge. Forms: R is p ÷ a = ? (answer the quotient), C is p ÷ ? = b (answer the divisor), S is ? ÷ a = b (answer the dividend); p = a × b, the times table read backwards, never ÷ 0, no 0 ÷ ? = 0. Divisors and quotients 0-12. T1 R: easy rows 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 11 × a digit, at least 8 with an 11 or 12. T2 R: 12 with 3, 4, 9 (at least 6), pairs of 3, 4, 9 (at least 6), pairs touching 3, 4, 9 from the core. T3 R: 11-12 facts with 6, 7, 8 or 11 × 11, 11 × 12, 12 × 12 (at least 8), pairs of 6, 7, 8 (at least 6). T4 C: core facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), core pairs of 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 (at least 8), a, b 2-12. T5 S: core facts 3-12 with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), any core fact 3-12 (at least 6), plus C (4 with an 11 or 12). Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least 2 near and at most 1 far. R: near within 2 of the quotient (GROUP_OFF q+-1, +-2), far SUBTRACTED p-a, MULTIPLIED p×a, TENS_SLIP q+-10. C: near within 2 of the divisor (MISSING_ONE_OFF a+-1, ARITH +-2), far MISSING_SUBTRACTED p-b, MISSING_MULTIPLIED p×b. S: near within the larger factor of the dividend (START_GROUP_OFF p+-a, START_ADDED a+b, START_TENS p+-10 when a factor is 11 or more, with a twin ones digit when p is 20 or more). The answer's rank among the four values is spread 15-35% per tier.

tiers.name: Easy facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the easy facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Building facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the next facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Harder facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the hardest plain facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Missing numbers
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷, a number missing: 4 + ? = 9, 12 ÷ ? = 3.

tiers.name: Missing first numbers
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷, often the first number missing: ? − 6 = 9.

ADD_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Count again: start at the bigger number and count up.
ADD_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted on wrong: the sum is one more or one less than the true sum.

ADD_SUBTRACTED.student: Plus means put together. Add the two numbers, don't take them apart.
ADD_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracted the smaller addend from the larger instead of adding: 8 + 5 = 3.

ADD_NO_CARRY.student: The ones made a new ten. Add that ten in with the tens.
ADD_NO_CARRY.teacher: Dropped the regrouped ten when the ones summed to 10 or more: 38 + 47 = 75.

ADD_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Add the tens, then the ones.
ADD_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Tens digit of the sum is one too many or too few, with the ones right: 34 + 52 = 76 or 96.

ADD_MISSING_ADDED.student: Don't add the two numbers you see. Find the missing one: subtract.
ADD_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: Added the shown number and the total instead of subtracting: 7 + ? = 15 answered 22.

ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Add your answer to the shown number and check the total.
ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted up wrong: the missing number is one more or one less than the true one.

ADD_MISSING_TENS.student: Check the tens. Add your answer to the shown number: is it the total?
ADD_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Missing number is ten too many or too few: forgot the trade counting up across a ten, or a tens slip.

SUB_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Check: answer + number taken away must equal the start.
SUB_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted back one step too many or too few: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 1.

SUB_ADDED.student: Take away, don't add. Subtracting makes the number smaller.
SUB_ADDED.teacher: Added the two numbers (s + a) instead of subtracting.

SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.student: You traded a ten for ones, so the tens digit has to drop by one.
SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.teacher: Regrouped the ones but left the tens unchanged: answer is 10 too big (14 - 6 gives 18; 52 - 38 gives 24).

SUB_TENS_SLIP.student: The tens are off by one ten. Check: answer + taken away = start.
SUB_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 10.

SUB_MISSING_ADDED.student: Add the missing part to what is left and you must get the start. Check it.
SUB_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: s - ? = b: added the two numbers shown (s + b) instead of finding what was taken away.

SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing number is one too big or too small (the answer plus or minus 1); did not check by substituting.

SUB_MISSING_TENS.student: Off by one ten. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: the missing number plus or minus 10 (trade forgotten or tens slip).

SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.student: The start is bigger than both numbers: add back what was taken away.
SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.teacher: ? - a = b: took the two shown numbers apart (|b - a|) instead of adding back what was taken.

SUB_START_NO_CARRY.student: Adding back, the ones made a ten: carry it. Check: start − taken = left.
SUB_START_NO_CARRY.teacher: ? - a = b: added the ones but dropped the carried ten, so the start is 10 too small.

MUL_GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
MUL_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

MUL_ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
MUL_ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

MUL_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
MUL_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.

DIV_GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
DIV_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

DIV_SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

DIV_MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

DIV_TENS_SLIP.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply back to check the size.
DIV_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Quotient off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: One off. Try your number in the problem: does the division work out?
DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing divisor off by one: stopped a fact early or late in the table.

DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Don't subtract. Ask: what times the answer shown makes the dividend?
DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts (p − b) to find the missing divisor instead of asking what times b makes p.

DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.student: One group off. Multiply the two numbers you see, no more, no less.
DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Missing dividend off by one divisor (a × (b +- 1)): counted one group too many or too few.

DIV_START_ADDED.student: Don't add. To undo dividing, multiply the two numbers you see.
DIV_START_ADDED.teacher: Adds the divisor and quotient (a + b) to find the missing dividend instead of multiplying back.

DIV_START_TENS.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply the two numbers, then check the size.
DIV_START_TENS.teacher: Missing dividend off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

items.explanation: 11 × 1 = 11: one group of 11. Any number times 1 is itself.
0 × 9 = 0: no groups, or groups of nothing, make 0. Anything times 0 is 0.
10 × 6 = 60: ten groups of 6, so put a zero after 6.
9 ÷ 3 = 3 because 3 × 3 = 9. Neighbour fact: 3 × 2 = 6, plus one more 3.
25 − 4 = 21: the ones are 5 − 4 = 1, the tens stay.
11 + 11 = 22: a double. Doubles are worth knowing by heart.
24 − 3 = 21: the ones are 4 − 3 = 1, the tens stay.
37 − 2 = 35: the ones are 7 − 2 = 5, the tens stay.
6 + 23 = 29: the tens stay, the ones go from 3 to 9.
43 + 6 = 49: the tens stay, the ones go from 3 to 9.
21 ÷ 3 = 7 because 3 × 7 = 21. Neighbour fact: 3 × 6 = 18, plus one more 3.
36 ÷ 4 = 9 because 4 × 9 = 36. Neighbour fact: 4 × 8 = 32, plus one more 4.
48 ÷ 6 = 8 because 6 × 8 = 48. Neighbour fact: 6 × 7 = 42, plus one more 6.
34 − 6: take 4 to get 30, then take 2 more: 28.
34 − 8: take 4 to get 30, then take 4 more: 26.
63 ÷ 7 = 9 because 7 × 9 = 63. Neighbour fact: 7 × 8 = 56, plus one more 7.
28 ÷ 4 = 7 because 4 × 7 = 28. Neighbour fact: 4 × 6 = 24, plus one more 4.
56 ÷ 7 = 8 because 7 × 8 = 56. Neighbour fact: 7 × 7 = 49, plus one more 7.
47 − 39: count up from 39 to 47, 8 steps. Check: 39 + 8 = 47.
30 − ? = 19: count up from 19 to 30, that is 11. So 30 − 11 = 19, ? = 11.
41 − ? = 25: count up from 25 to 41, that is 16. So 41 − 16 = 25, ? = 16.
8 × ? = 48: 8 × 6 = 48, so ? = 6. Count by 8s up to 48, or divide: 48 ÷ 8 = 6.
31 − ? = 18: count up from 18 to 31, that is 13. So 31 − 13 = 18, ? = 13.
8 × ? = 40: 8 × 5 = 40, so ? = 5. Count by 8s up to 40, or divide: 40 ÷ 8 = 5.
4 × ? = 20: 4 × 5 = 20, so ? = 5. Count by 4s up to 20, or divide: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
32 − ? = 28: count up from 28 to 32, that is 4. So 32 − 4 = 28, ? = 4.
6 × ? = 54: 6 × 9 = 54, so ? = 9. Count by 6s up to 54, or divide: 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
3 × ? = 36: 3 × 12 = 36, so ? = 12. Count by 3s up to 36, or divide: 36 ÷ 3 = 12.
43 − ? = 38: count up from 38 to 43, that is 5. So 43 − 5 = 38, ? = 5.
144 ÷ ? = 12: 12 × 12 = 144, so ? = 12. A square fact: 12 times itself makes 144.
? − 11 = 22: undo the take away, 22 + 11 = 33, so ? = 33. Check: 33 − 11 = 22.
25 − ? = 8: count up from 8 to 25, that is 17. So 25 − 17 = 8, ? = 17.
? × 6 = 72: 12 × 6 = 72, so ? = 12. Count by 6s up to 72, or divide: 72 ÷ 6 = 12.
8 × ? = 72: 8 × 9 = 72, so ? = 9. Count by 8s up to 72, or divide: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.
7 × ? = 56: 7 × 8 = 56, so ? = 8. Count by 7s up to 56, or divide: 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
49 ÷ ? = 7: 7 × 7 = 49, so ? = 7. A square fact: 7 times itself makes 49.
? − 4 = 37: undo the take away, 37 + 4 = 41, so ? = 41. Check: 41 − 4 = 37.
? × 4 = 24: 6 × 4 = 24, so ? = 6. Count by 4s up to 24, or divide: 24 ÷ 4 = 6.
